newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto warns media over coverage.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto warns media over coverage.

text.p: President Suharto on Wednesday warned the country's media not to imitate foreign press values in covering events in Indonesia.

"Any flow of information is usually followed by new values. Such values are sometimes unclear...but they are used or slipped into our media and widely spread among the people," Suharto said at a ceremony marking the country's press day.
"In this context, I am asking that we give attention to the values contained in the way the foreign press covers events in Indonesia," he added.
Suharto said some national media were using those foreign values.
"In fact, that way of thinking and those values are like glasses which colour our perception of ourselves and our surroundings," he said.

"The recent use of 'foreign glasses' has prompted the dramatisation of events... (and) conclusions which are drawn in a hurry or giving unbalanced coverage of the developments in our own country," he added.
Suharto said coverage by foreign media did not take into account Indonesian values.
"Because of the use of these incorrect glasses, it is understandable why many people in society become restless in facing change," he said.

Foreign press reports have included coverage of recent disturbances on the island of Java in which Moslem rioters have attacked Christian churches and homes and shops of ethnic Chinese. Local media have also reported the riots.
Political analysts say the government is increasingly aware of the impact of news reports on its image abroad and the potential effect on foreign investors.

Analysts have blamed the disturbances on social and economic tensions at a time of transition for Indonesia and questions over the presidential succession, with Suharto expected to seek another five-year term next year at the age of 76.
